output:
## Overview
Your chart is set with the Life Palace in Hai 亥 and the Body Palace in Wei 未, and your Five Element Bureau is Water 2. For a newcomer: the Life Palace is the anchor of the whole chart — the palace of your core temperament and the way you meet the world. The Body Palace is a second, complementary point, describing how that temperament shows up in action, especially from midlife onward. Here the Body Palace sits in the Wealth Palace, which tells you that doing, building and managing practical resources is where your character becomes visible.

What stands out most is the Life Palace in Hai holding Lian Zhen (the principled observer, sharp and discerning, here in its fallen brightness) together with Tan Lang (the charmer and connector, drawn to beauty, variety and experience, also fallen) — and Tan Lang carries Hua Lu (prosperity). A second signature is the pairing of Zi Wei (the emperor, dignified and status-conscious, brilliant) and Po Jun (the pioneer who clears the old to build the new, bright) in the Body Palace's Wealth Palace. Zuo Fu, the helpful deputy star, also sits in your Life Palace, and Huo Xing, a fast-moving challenging star, sits there too.

The overall picture is a sociable, resourceful, pleasure-and-beauty-loving surface over a distinctly capable, self-directed practical core. The two fallen stars in the Life Palace mean your charm and perceptiveness are strong but diffuse — they work best when given structure, and structure is exactly what Zi Wei and Po Jun in the Body Palace can supply.

## Life Palace and Personality
Your Life Palace in Hai holds Lian Zhen and Tan Lang, both fallen, with Tan Lang carrying Hua Lu. Lian Zhen is the discerning, principled observer with a taste for rules and clarity; Tan Lang is the charmer, the host, the one who wants to taste life rather than merely read about it. In fallen brightness, both tend to express as appetite without a container: many interests, many contacts, a strong pull toward enjoyment, and sometimes a wavering between wanting freedom and wanting recognition. Hua Lu on Tan Lang is significant — it places a prosperity transformation right on your core star, which traditionally points to sociability and a knack for drawing opportunity toward you through people and presence. The risk is treating that ease as enough; the opportunity is making it deliberate.

Zuo Fu in the Life Palace is genuine support: helpful people, practical assistance and a sense of being backed when you ask. Huo Xing in the same palace adds speed and impatience — a quick temper that flares and clears. Channel it as drive: short bursts of decisive action suit you better than slow, grinding routines, provided you finish what the burst starts. The Body Palace's presence in the Wealth Palace is worth noting on its own: your identity is closely tied to what you build and own, and you tend to feel most yourself when engaged in concrete work.

The Life Palace faces the Travel Palace, which is empty and borrows Lian Zhen and Tan Lang from the Life Palace itself, so the outer-world expression of your personality largely mirrors the inner one — you present much as you are, with little hiding. The practical takeaway: give your many interests one or two committed containers (a craft, a discipline, a community role) and let Zuo Fu's support and Hua Lu's sociability work inside them rather than scattering them.

## Career
Your Career Palace in Mao holds Wu Qu (the disciplined executor, the one who values method and results, in fair brightness) and Qi Sha (the determined general, bold and unyielding, bright). This is a strong working combination: Qi Sha supplies ambition and willingness to take on difficult assignments, while Wu Qu supplies the follow-through and respect for standards. You are likely well suited to roles with real responsibility and measurable outcomes, and less happy in purely supportive or vague positions.

You Bi sits in the Career Palace and carries Hua Ke (recognition) from your birth year — a genuinely useful placement, suggesting that reputation and being noticed for competence come through the workplace and through the people who vouch for you. Wu Qu and Qi Sha have no brightness shortfall worth worrying about, but their energy is direct and can read as blunt; learning to sequence your decisiveness — listening first, deciding second — is the main working skill to develop.

The Career Palace faces the Spouse Palace, which holds Tian Fu (the steady treasurer, calm and dependable, bright). Your working life and your close partnerships are linked: a settled home base tends to make your professional boldness safer, and professional intensity can strain that base if it crowds it. Worth watching: the pull to take on one more demanding project when the honest answer is that capacity is full.

## Wealth
Your Wealth Palace in Wei is also your Body Palace, and it holds Zi Wei (the emperor, dignified and status-conscious, brilliant) and Po Jun (the pioneer, bright). This is one of the most vivid placements in your chart: money and resources are tied to your sense of standing and to your willingness to break and rebuild. Zi Wei wants quality, recognition and the best available; Po Jun is restless with the status quo and tends to make changes — sometimes before the old structure has fully wound down. Together they suggest someone who earns through initiative and renewal rather than through quiet accumulation, and who does best when a dignified standard (Zi Wei) governs the pioneer's impulses (Po Jun).

Tian Yue, a helpful-people star, sits in the Wealth Palace — support and timely assistance tend to arrive through relationships, which makes your network a real resource in practical matters. The challenging side here is not in the Wealth Palace itself but in the Life Palace's Huo Xing: a fast appetite for the new can outrun careful review. A useful practice is a written pause before any large commitment — one week, a second opinion, a review of what you already hold.

The Wealth Palace faces the Wellbeing Palace, which holds Tian Xiang (the minister, calm and fair-minded, brilliant) plus Tian Kui, Ling Xing, Di Kong and Di Jie. That inner-life palace carries a lot of both support and static, and its message for wealth is that your financial peace depends on your inner peace — when your mind is crowded, spending decisions get crowded too.

## Love and Partnership
Your Spouse Palace in You holds Tian Fu, bright, with no transformation and no other main star. Tian Fu is the treasurer: steady, reliable, quietly generous, preferring calm to drama. This suggests a partnership style in which stability, loyalty and practical care matter more than grand gestures — you are more likely to thrive with someone consistent and grounded than with someone whose appeal is intensity. It also suggests you may be the steadier party in some relationships, or that you look for a partner who acts as a stable base for your more pioneering side.

Di Jie, one of the challenging stars, sits in the Spouse Palace. Read it as a texture rather than a warning: it points to a tendency toward interruptions in the rhythm of partnership — separate schedules, differing expectations, or a habit of renegotiating terms — that needs patient, explicit conversation rather than assumption. Partners who can talk plainly about practical arrangements tend to do better with this placement than those who leave things unspoken. The Spouse Palace faces the Career Palace, so professional demands and relationship needs should be planned together rather than treated as separate compartments.

Because your Life Palace stars are sociable and your Body Palace is in the Wealth Palace, there is a pull to let work and social life absorb the time that partnership needs. A concrete habit worth building: one recurring, protected block of time together that does not move when work intensifies.

## Wellbeing Habits
Your Health Palace in Wu holds Tian Ji (the strategist, quick-thinking and analytical, brilliant) carrying Hua Ji (obstacle), with Qing Yang, a sharp challenging star, also there. This combination points to a mind that runs constantly — overthinking, planning, reworking problems — and to a tendency for that mental activity to spill into restlessness and tension held in the body. The practical cue is to treat rest as a discipline, not a reward: a consistent wind-down before sleep, fewer screens late, and a clear end to the working day.

For food and movement, the Life Palace's Tan Lang and fallen Lian Zhen suggest an appetite-led style — enjoyment matters to you, and rigid restriction tends not to hold. Better to work with variety and quality rather than austerity: interesting, well-prepared meals in reasonable portions, and movement that feels like play or challenge rather than penance. Wu Qu and Qi Sha in the Career Palace favor structured, strength-oriented activity; Huo Xing in the Life Palace favors short, vigorous sessions over long, slow ones.

For emotional balance, the key is the gap between your fast inner commentary (Tian Ji) and your actual capacity. A simple regular practice — journalling, a walk without a plan, or talking something through with someone you trust — helps discharge the mental loop before it settles into the body. Give yourself permission to do less on days when the inner strategist is loud.

If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Family and Social Circle
Your Friends Palace in Chen holds Tai Yang (the sun, generous and public-facing, bright) with Tuo Luo, a challenging star, in the same palace. Tai Yang in a social palace suggests a wide, visible circle and a tendency to be the one who lights things up — you may be the connector in your group. Tuo Luo tends to slow things down: some friendships or collaborations progress at a pace you find frustrating, or take a long time to mature. The workable response is patience and clarity about who does what; giving connections time rather than pushing them often turns out better than forcing momentum.

The Siblings Palace in Xu holds Tai Yin (the moon, gentle and receptive, bright) carrying Hua Quan (power). Hua Quan here suggests that siblings can have real influence in your life — sometimes as the one who takes charge, sometimes as the one whose authority you feel. Tai Yin softens this: the tone is more likely to be caring and quietly decisive than confrontational. Keep decisions among siblings explicit, since Hua Quan can drift into unspoken hierarchy.

The Parents Palace in Zi holds Ju Men (the advocate, sharp-tongued and argumentative, bright), and Wen Chang, a talent-and-learning star, sits there too. This points to a family background where talk, debate and study were prominent — a home where opinions were voiced, and where written or intellectual expression was valued. Ju Men's edge means disagreements with parents or elders may be verbal and quick; choosing the right moment to raise something matters more than the strength of the argument.

In the Children Palace, which is empty and borrows Tian Tong (the gentle optimist, easygoing and kind, fair) and Tian Liang (the elder, principled and protective, brilliant) from the Property Palace: with younger people and with any children in your life, you tend to show up as a warm, protective, slightly mentoring presence. Your Property Palace itself holds those same two stars plus Wen Qu, a writing-and-aesthetics star, suggesting that a home filled with books, conversation and comfort suits you well.

## Major Period and Year by Year
Your current Major Period (ages 22 to 31 in East Asian counting) falls in the Spouse Palace in You, holding Tian Fu in bright brightness. The focus of these ten years is partnership, commitment and the practical arrangements that hold close relationships together — contracts in the broadest sense. Tian Fu's steady character means the pace here is generally unhurried and consolidating rather than dramatic; it suits building something durable, whether that is a partnership, a home base, or a working alliance. Di Jie in this same palace asks for patience when plans get interrupted. The next Major Period, ages 32 to 41, moves to the Children Palace in Shen, an empty palace that borrows Tian Tong and Tian Liang from the Property Palace — a shift toward warmth, mentorship, home and the next generation, with a gentler pace than your current period.

Each annual pillar follows the Chinese lunar year and roughly matches the calendar year.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu
The annual Life Palace falls in your Health Palace, where Tian Ji in brilliant brightness carries Hua Ji. The tone for the year leans toward mental activity, analysis and self-scrutiny — a year that rewards reflection but can leave you overthinking. The year's transformations: Tian Tong carries Hua Lu in the Property Palace, which points to home, property matters and family comfort as worth leaning into; Tian Ji carries Hua Quan in the Health Palace, giving genuine drive toward improving routines; Wen Chang carries Hua Ke in the Parents Palace, favoring study, writing and good relations with elders or mentors. Lian Zhen carries Hua Ji in your Life Palace, so the area calling for care is your own core energy and self-presentation — moments of irritation or blurting something out are better handled by pausing than by pressing on.

Combined with the Major Period's focus on partnership, this year is well suited to settling practical matters around home and relationship, and less suited to pushing hard on personal reinvention. Early in the year is a good time to establish routines; in the second half, protect your energy around demanding social situations.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei
The annual Life Palace now falls in your Wealth Palace, bringing Zi Wei and Po Jun into the foreground of the year — a period suited to initiative, practical decisions and scenarios where you are building or renewing something. The transformations: Tai Yin carries Hua Lu in the Siblings Palace, pointing toward siblings and close peers as sources of support and warmth; Tian Tong carries Hua Quan in the Property Palace, giving real momentum to home and property matters; Tian Ji carries Hua Ke in the Health Palace, favoring thoughtful self-care and study of your own habits; Ju Men carries Hua Ji in the Parents Palace, where communication with parents or elders calls for extra care — sharp words are better left unsaid in the moment.

With the Major Period still on partnership, this year's money-minded energy is best aimed at shared goals rather than solitary ones. In the first half, lean into supportive family and peer relationships; in the second half, handle any delicate family conversations slowly.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen
The annual Life Palace falls in the Children Palace, which is empty and borrows Tian Tong and Tian Liang from the Property Palace. This gives a warm, protective, slightly mentoring tone to the year — good for younger people, creative projects and a gentler pace. The transformations: Tan Lang carries Hua Lu in your Life Palace, lifting sociability and charm; Tai Yin carries Hua Quan in the Siblings Palace again, giving quiet influence among peers; You Bi carries Hua Ke in the Career Palace, favoring recognition at work and support from colleagues; Tian Ji carries Hua Ji in the Health Palace, so the same mental-overload theme asks for care. Note that the Major Period this year is still the Spouse Palace, so balancing the pull toward the wider world with commitment at home is the year's central task.

Summer is a good time to put energy into creative or mentoring projects; toward the end of the year, keep your schedule lighter to protect rest.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You
The annual Life Palace now coincides with your Spouse Palace, bringing Tian Fu in bright brightness directly into focus and doubling its significance, since this is also your Major Period palace. Partnership, commitment and practical arrangements come to the fore. The transformations: Wu Qu carries Hua Lu in the Career Palace, favoring disciplined professional progress; Tan Lang carries Hua Quan in the Life Palace, giving personal presence and influence; Tian Liang carries Hua Ke in the Property Palace, supporting home and family decisions; Wen Qu carries Hua Ji in the Property Palace, where planning, documents and domestic details call for a slower pace and a second review.

This is a year for careful, patient building rather than expansion. Spring is a good time to address written or practical commitments; autumn rewards patience when domestic details feel tedious.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu
The annual Life Palace moves to the Siblings Palace, where Tai Yin carries Hua Quan in brilliant brightness — a year in which close peers, siblings and peer networks have real weight. The transformations: Tai Yang carries Hua Lu in the Friends Palace, favoring your wider social circle and being visible among groups; Wu Qu carries Hua Quan in the Career Palace again, supporting steady professional effort; Tai Yin carries Hua Ke in the Siblings Palace, a good placement for warm, clear peer relationships; Tian Tong carries Hua Ji in the Property Palace, where home and property matters benefit from care and unhurried attention.

This year also marks the transition into your next Major Period (ages 32 to 41, in the Children Palace), a gentler, more mentoring phase. In the first half, put time into friendships and groups; in the second half, pace yourself as new responsibilities and a shift in personal focus begin to settle in.

## Guidance
- Give your Life Palace's Tan Lang and Lian Zhen a container: pick one or two committed disciplines or communities and put your social energy into them, rather than spreading it across many. This turns Hua Lu's prosperity into something lasting.
- Sit one week on any large decision. Your Huo Xing in the Life Palace and Po Jun in the Body Palace favor quick, decisive moves; a written pause protects you from acting on appetite.
- Make one required, recurring block of time for partnership that does not move when work intensifies. This works directly with Tian Fu in the Spouse Palace and Di Jie's tendency to create interruptions.
- Build a wind-down routine before sleep. Tian Ji carrying Hua Ji in your Health Palace with Qing Yang points to a mind that needs a clear stopping point.
- Accept help when it is offered. Zuo Fu in the Life Palace and Tian Yue in the Wealth Palace both indicate that support comes through people — letting yourself use it is a practical habit, not a weakness.
